FORMAL SAFETY VERIFICATION OF ROBOTIC-MATTER VEHICLES AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:智能機器人物質車輛的形式化安全驗證極限 27/90 FORMAL SAFETY VERIFICATION OF ROBOTIC-MATTER VEHICLES AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy, Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 27 of 90. It asks whether an unoccupied, reconfigurable robotic-matter body panel can preserve precisely specified load-bearing, identity, control, and physical-stop invariants through all permitted shape transitions. The core three-coupling is Formal Verification x Reconfigurable Systems x Safety Boundaries. The book proposes conditional proofs and experimentally refutable engineering contracts, not a roadworthy passenger vehicle, type approval, or validated automotive safety certification. Its central hypothesis is falsifiable. Under equal material, time, sensing, reference, energy, computation and human-operation budgets, a preregistered formal-verification-and-runtime-assurance architecture should improve physical identity continuity without worsening independent replay completeness relative to professionally configured fleet telemetry, expert inspection and capable classical safeguards. Blind challenges include unlogged module replacements, calibration loss, shared sensor bias, unsupported load paths, illegal intermediate configurations, stale software proofs, communication partitions and real actuator stop delays. A mathematical claim fails at the system boundary whenever the actual physical plant violates its stated assumptions or the independent veto cannot be exercised. Thirty different mathematical research plates examine covariance propagation, inductive invariants, hybrid automata, forward reachability, control barrier functions, rigidity and contact-force constraints, buckling, fatigue, temporal logic, consensus, observability, set-valued inference, innovation calibration, statistical false-clear bounds, Bayesian updates, model abstraction soundness, deadline schedulability, stop-energy reserves and conjunctive permission. Each plate supplies its actual mathematical construction, units or types, validity conditions, a sealed disconfirmation experiment and chapter interfaces. The source's uncertainty-propagation candidate u_y^2 = J Sigma_x J^T + u_model^2 is preserved while explaining why uncertainty quantification alone does not constitute a formal vehicle-safety proof. Eighty-two chapters hold 410 single-page investigations across proof-domain definition, physical structural invariants, distributed control, measurement identifiability, blinded counterexamples, and cross-generational requalification. Two hundred individually specified Research Gates demand explicit physical observables, rival explanations, complete negative cases and reproducible stop conditions. Thirty-three genuinely different Phoenix Answer Embryos propose future proof tools, physical truth fixtures, timing witnesses, identity ledgers and successor-ready scientific interfaces; none is described as a constructed or tested product. Evidence ancestry retains author-supplied Flagship 13 DOIs (10.5281/zenodo.23318840; 10.5281/zenodo.23318839; metadata not independently confirmed) and distinguishes established formal-methods precedent: the autonomous robotics verification survey (10.1145/3342355), differential dynamic logic for hybrid systems (10.1007/s10817-008-9103-8), control barrier functions for safety-critical control (10.1109/TAC.2016.2638961), and symbolic verification of embedded systems (10.1109/32.489079). Relevant inspection and digital twin methods are cited with their original scope. None establishes a working F27 robotic-matter vehicle or passenger-safety capability. Mathematical expert review, full semantic duplication audit, and independent experimental validation remain outstanding.
